# Numerical Feature Extraction {#sec-numerical-feature-extraction}
FLIM Playground extracts *single-cell* numerical features from **multiple channels and imaging modalities in the same workflow**. Configure each channel independently: give it a name, choose FLIM or intensity-only imaging, and select the [feature extractors](data_extraction_config.qmd#feature-extractor) needed for that channel. For example, a FLIM channel can provide lifetime and phasor features while an intensity-only channel provides morphology and texture. All channels can also be intensity-only. FLIM channels share the [FLIM input format](data_extraction_config.qmd#decay-types), but their feature selections can differ.

**An IRF shift is required for raw FLIM channels using `Lifetime fit`, and for channels using `Lifetime fit free` with `IRF` calibration.** Complete [IRF Calibration](irf_calibration.qmd#sec-irf-calibration) for those channels or load metadata with saved shifts. Calibration with a fluorescence lifetime standard (calibration dye) is applied during phasor extraction. All-intensity workflows proceed directly to extraction.

The available feature extractors are:

- [Lifetime fit](#sec-lifetime-fit): fit exponential models to raw decay curves to estimate lifetimes and their fractional contributions, or read existing fitted values from pre-fitted FLIM input.
- [Lifetime fit free](#sec-lifetime-fit-free): transform decay curves to phasor space using Fourier transform to obtain phasor coordinates. 
- [Intensity Morphology](#sec-intensity-morphology): morphological features of single-cell ROI masks
- [Intensity Texture](#sec-intensity-texture): texture features of single-cell ROI intensity images (or, for 2D decay input, just the per-cell decay-curve sum, `intensity_sum`)

## Input 

A CSV file extracted in the [fov metadata extraction](#sec-fov-metadata) step that contains the metadata of the FOVs including: 

- [required file paths](fov_metadata.qmd#fov-file-paths)
- [decay type](fov_metadata.qmd#decay-type)
- [decay info](fov_metadata.qmd#decay-info)
- [selected feature extractors](fov_metadata.qmd#feature-extractors) for each channel
- [fit free calibration method](data_extraction_config.qmd#calibration-method) (if fit free calibration is required)

Use the cached metadata just exported in [FOV Metadata Extraction](#sec-fov-metadata), or upload a previously saved metadata CSV. Cached metadata takes precedence; refresh the page to clear it and upload a different file.

## Feature Extraction

Click **Confirm and Start** to extract the selected features. For channels that need an IRF shift, first [confirm calibration](irf_calibration.qmd#confirm-calibration) or load metadata with saved shifts. For raw FLIM channels using `Lifetime fit`, choose the fitting mode before starting.

The right side of the screen lists the fields of view and their extraction status. Each FOV has a progress bar while it is being processed; completed FOVs show their result badges. Keep this view open to follow the batch.

![Full extraction screen: Mosaic01–03 are complete while Mosaic07 is processing.](extraction_ui_shots/numerical_feature_extraction.png){width=100% fig-align=center fig-alt="Full Numeric Feature Extraction screen with the workflow and Local fitting controls on the left, successful Mosaic01–03 badges, and an active NADH extraction progress bar for 40 cells in Mosaic07 on the right."}

![This numerical extraction example produces 185 cell rows and 70 columns from one FOV.](extraction_ui_shots/feature_export.png){width=100% fig-align=center fig-alt="Successful extraction for MCF7_2DG_dish2_04, a preview of the first five cell rows, and the Download single cell features as CSV button."}

The completed result above includes a preview of the extracted cell table.

Warnings are displayed if cells have `NaN` values for some features. They are *not* excluded from the final CSV file. 

## Save Results

Once the feature extraction is finished, the results are saved to a CSV file. How this happens depends on how the metadata reached this step. If the cached metadata file from the [fov metadata extraction](#sec-fov-metadata) step was used, the CSV is written automatically into the same folder as that metadata file, and no button is shown. If the metadata file was uploaded manually, FLIM Playground cannot know where to write it, so a `Download single cell features as CSV` button appears at the bottom of the page instead.
